Chirality is a local-first desktop harness for running governed AI agents against a user-selected filesystem workspace.
Chirality bundles a release-managed instruction root inside the app, lets the user select a mutable working root, and uses plain files plus git history as the durable substrate for professional work.
Core insight: if the filesystem is the database, architecture is a state-and-authority specification, not a service mesh.
Chirality exists to accelerate deliverable-heavy professional work by organizing agent activity around packages, deliverables, dependencies, lifecycle files, and review gates.
Chirality exists to make AI-assisted work auditable, reviewable, and controllable where provenance, human accountability, and traceability matter.
Chirality exists to keep humans in charge of every binding decision while agents perform drafting, extraction, reconciliation, scaffolding, summarization, and routine transformation.
Chirality exists to provide a desktop harness whose product identity is Chirality, not a vendor CLI, SDK, cloud workflow, or hidden database.
Chirality exists to preserve a path from interactive assistance to governed deliverable production without implying automated professional approval.

Chirality is not just a chat wrapper; it is a governed work harness combining local filesystem truth, agent instructions, deterministic tools, runtime auditability, human gates, and a professional-responsibility posture.
Project state is represented as human-readable files under the working root, with no required external database, hidden server, or vendor-hosted project memory.
Nodes are package folders, deliverable folders, domain profile folders, proposal folders, and tool-root snapshots.
Edges are Dependencies.csv rows, lifecycle references, traceability references, operation proposals, and review records.

Properties are markdown and CSV files such as _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, Dependencies.csv, Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, and session event logs.
Agents and tools may traverse filesystem state but do not replace it; when a fact matters for reliance, it must land in the appropriate versioned project file or approved artifact.

Git history is the durable event store for accepted project state, providing reviewable diffs, rollback, traceability, and auditability independent of chat history, vendor transcripts, runtime caches, or UI state.
If a decision is not in a versioned file, it does not exist for purposes of reliance.
Runtime session logs explain what happened during agent work and are important audit records, but are not a substitute for accepted project-state files and human approval records.

Chirality runtime events record accepted turns, provider/SDK messages, model deltas, permission decisions, tool calls, hook outcomes, compaction boundaries, subagent lifecycle, failures, interruptions, and terminal outcomes, supporting replay, diagnosis, and review.
The canonical Chirality runtime audit mirror is .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl or an explicitly configured Chirality-controlled session path.
External SDK transcripts are secondary runtime artifacts unless imported into Chirality's event schema.
Runtime events do not make a deliverable approved, issued, code-compliant, externally validated, or safe for reliance.
Gate-relevant decisions must be represented in versioned project files and accepted by an accountable human.
Agents propose; humans approve. Professional responsibility is personal, non-transferable, and not delegated to a model, tool, SDK, runtime, or deterministic validator.

Only humans may author binding approval records, approve issue/release actions, select governing standards, accept residual risk, adjudicate source conflicts requiring judgment, and decide whether work may be relied upon.
Approvals bind to specific content and must be traceable to a git SHA or equivalent immutable evidence; content changes after approval void the approval until reviewed again.
Chirality values evidence over fluent output and must prefer source-backed statements, explicit assumptions, and visible uncertainty over plausible invention.
Required posture: cite or record source paths for extracted dependencies and important claims.
Required posture: label assumptions as ASSUMPTION, proposals as PROPOSAL, unknowns as TBD, and observed facts as FACT where practical.
Required posture: surface conflicts rather than silently resolving them.
Required posture: prefer 'location TBD' over fabricated provenance.
Required posture: use deterministic tools for validation, parsing, scaffolding, linting, and repeatable transformations when available.

No hidden memory may become authoritative project state; UI drafts, local presets, SDK transcripts, model context, runtime logs, app caches, API keys, and provider transcripts are non-authoritative unless a governed process imports their content into the project filesystem.

Convenience state is permitted when explicitly non-authoritative and unable to override governance; examples include UI pane widths, local runtime presets, API key storage, draft chat text, and SDK resume metadata.
Chirality separates the release-managed instruction root from the mutable working root.

The instruction root is bundled app resources such as AGENTS.md, agents/, docs/, framework guidance, and release-managed instructions; it is read-only during ordinary project execution and updated only by release/governance changes.

The working root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local filesystem path where project execution state, deliverables, sessions, and tool artifacts live; it is mutable under runtime policy and human gates.
The instruction root defines how agents should behave; the working root contains the project being worked on; these roots must not be conflated.

Reliance boundaries must be documented, implemented, and tested in Chirality terms and must not depend on prompt text or opaque SDK defaults alone.
When SDK hooks or callbacks enforce a boundary, Chirality must be able to verify the enforcement path and record the result.

Chirality may use external engines, libraries, and APIs but must not become a Claude Code wrapper in identity, copy, behavior, or governance.

Structural constraint: deny-first permission semantics, so a deny from policy, hook, path check, governance, or human gate overrides any allow.
Structural constraint: runtime code enforces safety; prompt instructions reinforce policy but are not sufficient enforcement.
Structural constraint: MCP is a transport, not a bypass; in-process MCP tools must pass through the same policy as SDK built-ins.
Structural constraint: product identity stays Chirality; the app must not present itself as a vendor CLI or external product.
Structural constraint: domain engines own domain truth; Chirality governs interaction and records but does not become the solver.

The vNext runtime is provider-adapter-general, contract-owned, and Chirality-governed: adapters supply reusable machinery only where verified while Chirality defines reliance boundaries, configures the engine, records what happened, and preserves governed exit paths.

The desktop and harness shell are substantially scaffolded: typed API routes, JSON session records, attachment validation, provider selection, subagent governance, network guardrails, API-key handling, UI surfaces, and Section 8 validation exist.

The harness is not yet a full governed agent runtime; it is mostly a provider streaming adapter where opts.tools is not backed by a real tool surface, permission behavior is partly simulated, there is no append-only per-turn Chirality transcript, and the Next.js turn route owns too much runtime lifecycle.
The next development objective is to evolve the shell into a governed provider-adapter Chirality runtime without becoming a thin Claude Code wrapper or any other external harness wrapper.

The first implementation slice must establish a thin TurnEngine wrapper around the first adapter, adapter option construction, provider/SDK-message mapping, append-only Chirality session events, redacted run logging, first-adapter settings isolation, prompt composition, and an explicit AgentEnginePort/RuntimeEngineContract boundary without changing the browser-facing SSE contract.

Local tool exposure should begin by configuring first-adapter SDK built-ins and in-process Chirality MCP tools behind capability-forward policy with explicit hard-deny precedence, not by building a custom model/tool loop from scratch.

A custom runtime remains an explicit fallback if the R0/R1 first-adapter probe proves the adapter cannot satisfy, expose, or be wrapped to satisfy a product-critical Chirality requirement without weakening governance.

The Professional Operator is a licensed professional, project lead, or accountable reviewer who needs AI-assisted production while retaining decision rights; they select the working root, approve gates, review evidence, and decide what can be relied upon.

The Project Orchestrator converts a scope of work into packages, deliverables, lifecycle records, document kits, dependency registers, and coordination artifacts using ORCHESTRATOR, WORKING_ITEMS, RECONCILIATION, CHANGE, and PIPELINE lanes.
The Specialist Contributor is a user or workflow that executes bounded deliverable-local work through TASK, DEPENDENCIES, CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK, CHIRALITY_LENS, ESTIMATING, or audit agents.

The Governance Maintainer is responsible for agent instruction conformance, invariant consistency, deterministic tooling, permission modes, runtime policies, and release-managed instruction root changes.
The Release Operator builds, validates, packages, verifies instruction-root inclusion, and distributes local unsigned desktop builds.
The Harness Runtime Maintainer is responsible for TurnEngine, event schema, tool contracts, permission policy, provider adapters, result storage, context compaction, and validation evolution.

The Future Domain Engine Integrator defines Domain Engine Profiles, deterministic adapters, protected path rules, manifest requirements, and operation-proposal workflows; this role appears only after the harness runtime spine, permissions, tools, hooks, and result storage are stable.

The Future Domain Reviewer is an accountable reviewer who examines domain-engine proposals, deterministic results, provenance, and professional-boundary notices before any accepted domain state changes.
Principle: filesystem is the database - project state is represented as human-readable files under the working root.
Principle: git is the event store for project truth - review, audit, rollback, and approvals bind to git-tracked content.
Principle: runtime events are an audit trail, not project truth; session logs explain what happened but gate-relevant decisions must still land in versioned project files.
Principle: human authority at every gate - agents propose; humans approve, issue, sign, seal, and decide.
Principle: evidence over plausibility - claims require provenance, and unknowns become TBD, not guesses.
Principle: no hidden memory for project truth - runtime convenience state is allowed only when explicitly non-authoritative.
Principle: instruction root and working root are separate - release-managed agent OS files must not be modified by project execution.
Principle: provider-adapter-general, contract-owned - provider SDKs may supply generic agent-loop mechanics, but Chirality owns the runtime contract exposed to the app and to project governance.

Principle: reliance boundaries are first-class - audit, permission, lifecycle, filesystem-truth, transcript-canonicality, and human-gate semantics must be defined and tested in Chirality terms, not inferred from provider/SDK defaults.
Principle: engine replaceability by construction - every adapter must sit behind explicit contracts, conformance tests, and fallback criteria so upstream changes do not silently redefine the product.
Principle: SDK isolation - shipped builds must not load ambient user/global Claude Code settings; programmatic options and Chirality instruction-root policy are the source of runtime behavior.

Principle: provider-neutral core - core runtime records, APIs, and tests use Chirality terms; Claude/SDK-specific identifiers, message names, transcript paths, permission modes, and tool names are translated at the adapter boundary.
Principle: routes stay thin - HTTP routes parse requests, handle transport, acquire/release locks, and forward events, while runtime services own behavior.
Principle: persist accepted user input early - a killed or interrupted process must leave a recoverable accepted-turn record.
Principle: separate UI events from runtime events - browser UIEvents remain stable and compact while persisted runtime events may be richer and versioned.
Principle: expose only policy-permitted capabilities to the model - tool-surface resolution happens before adapter request construction, and allowedTools alone is not enough.

Principle: hard denies override allows - provider/SDK deny rules, hook denials, path-containment failures, protected-path rules, release/professional boundaries, and governance denials override any allow decision.
Principle: safety lives in runtime code - prompts reinforce safety but do not replace path containment, permission policy, hooks, result budgets, timeouts, and packaging/network controls.
Principle: MCP is a transport, not a bypass - in-process Chirality MCP tools must pass through the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event-logging policy as SDK built-ins.
Principle: product identity stays Chirality - SDK usage must not make the app look, behave, or describe itself as Claude Code.
Principle: immutable snapshots - snapshot-producing runs create timestamped folders that are not overwritten, though _LATEST.md pointers may move.
Principle: least structure that works - rigor scales with stakes and structure is added when it reduces error, rework, or ambiguity.
Principle: extensibility follows maturity - remote MCP, plugins, broad tool search, and remote execution are later-phase capabilities gated by stable local SDK integration and Chirality governance.
Principle: domain engines own domain truth - when a domain engine is integrated, Chirality governs interaction, proposals, records, and human gates but does not become the solver.
Principle: fixtures are not core - OpenPipeStress may be the first useful Domain Engine Profile fixture, but its assumptions belong in profile and adapter layers rather than Chirality core runtime.

Working-root selection journey: the app validates that the path exists, is a directory, is readable/writable, and is not inside the instruction root.
Working-root selection journey: the app stores the selected root as local UI state and uses it for file tree, scan, chat session, scaffold, and contract APIs.

Working-root selection acceptance: relative paths are rejected, missing/inaccessible directories show actionable errors, instruction-root conflicts are blocked, and clearing the root disables runtime actions requiring projectRoot.
Agent matrix navigation: selecting a NORMATIVE or EVALUATIVE cell routes to WORKBENCH with agent context; selecting an OPERATIVE cell routes to PIPELINE with category context.
Agent matrix navigation: if deliverables are present, clicking a deliverable row routes to PIPELINE TASK* with that deliverable preselected.
Agent matrix acceptance: disabled or unsupported variants remain visible as coming soon rather than silently disappearing.

Scaffold journey: the app calls POST /api/harness/scaffold and the runtime parses package/deliverable tables, creates tool roots, copies decomposition, writes INIT.md and _Coordination/_COORDINATION.md, creates packages and deliverable folders, and returns validation summaries.

Scaffold acceptance: scaffolding is idempotent for existing directories/files, failures are fail-fast with stage/target-path/created-paths for recovery, and PREPARATION compatibility is reported before the user proceeds.

Workbench persona session journey: the chat panel resolves persona aliases to instruction-file names, the runtime persists turn.accepted before calling the model, streams turn events to the UI, and the user may interrupt the turn.

Workbench persona session acceptance: session identity is preserved across turns for the same root/persona/mode, runtime errors preserve the draft and attachments for retry, interrupt returns a terminal process:exit event, and persisted events can reconstruct accepted turns/deltas/outcome/interruption status.

Operative pipeline journey: the user selects DECOMP, PREP, TASK, or AUDIT, then a category-specific agent or lane; for TASK the user selects scope mode and dynamic scope from the working root, and inspects deliverable status/dependency snapshots applying allowed lifecycle transitions.

Operative pipeline acceptance: deliverable selections reset when project root or scan results become stale, KNOWLEDGE_TYPES mode shows only when a knowledge decomposition marker is detected, and lifecycle transitions enforce authorized actors and approval-SHA requirements for human gate states.

Attachment journey: the UI previews attachments as non-authoritative client metadata, the server validates/classifies/reads attachments, and the turn proceeds if user text exists or at least one valid attachment resolves.
Attachment acceptance: allowed extensions are .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .pdf, .txt, .md, .csv.
Attachment acceptance: symlinks, directories, special files, unsupported extensions, unreadable files, files over 10 MB, and total raw bytes over 18 MB are rejected.
Attachment acceptance: partial attachment failure is non-fatal when executable content remains, and if all attachments fail with empty text the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE.

API key journey: the user stores a key through Electron IPC, Electron encrypts key material with safeStorage outside the working root, and the server runtime reads the UI key from process global or falls back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

API key acceptance: key material is never written to working-root files, UI key takes precedence over env keys, API key status reports source as ui/env/none, and if secure storage is unavailable the UI reports an error.

Permissioned read tool journey: the runtime resolves the tool pool exposing only permitted read tools, validates input, checks path containment and symlink policy, records the permission decision, executes the tool, stores/summarizes the result, and feeds it back to the model.

Permissioned read tool acceptance: read tool execution appears in both SSE and persisted runtime events, denied/malformed calls do not execute, and large outputs are previewed and stored under session artifacts rather than flooding chat.

Controlled write/edit journey: the runtime exposes write tools only if mode/permission rules allow or can ask, validates target path under working root, rejects instruction-root and (initially) symlink writes, requires exact edit preconditions, requests approval when policy requires ask, and performs atomic write/edit emitting a diff/summary.

Controlled write/edit acceptance: readOnly mode cannot write, dontAsk denies unapproved writes and bash actions, explicit deny rules override session/operator allows, and write/edit operations are auditable through runtime events and project git diffs.

Resume-after-failure journey: when a process is interrupted or fails after input is accepted, runtime event replay shows the accepted turn and terminal failure/cancellation status when the user later opens session history.

Resume-after-failure acceptance: accepted user input is recoverable even if no model token was produced, malformed trailing JSONL writes do not break listing or replay of valid prior events, and session metadata remains usable for listing and resume.

Governed subagent delegation journey: the runtime evaluates evaluateSubagentGovernance as the authoritative gate, requiring environment enablement, persona allowlist, context sealing, pipeline approval, approval reference, and Type 2 task-agent eligibility, and in a later phase creates a child run record with restricted tools/cwd streaming lifecycle to the parent session.

Governed subagent delegation acceptance: delegation without governance metadata is denied, delegation to a non-allowlisted or non-Type-2 candidate is denied, and the parent session records child lifecycle and output artifact path when execution support exists.

Validate-and-package journey: the release operator installs dependencies in frontend/, runs tests/typecheck/harness validation, runs the desktop distribution build, and the build packages app resources and verifies instruction-root integrity.

Validate-and-package acceptance: frontend/dist/Chirality-0.1.0-arm64.dmg is produced for macOS arm64, the app bundle includes expected instruction-root resources, the minimum macOS target is 15.0.0 or later, and the build is unsigned/adhoc by design.

Additional SSE tool progress events may be introduced only with UI compatibility handling.

The SSE stream must always terminate with a process-level completion/error signal unless the client disconnects and cancel cleanup runs; client disconnect cleanup records cancellation in the persisted runtime log once it exists.

SSE adapter requirement: provider/SDK messages are not the browser contract; the first-adapter sdk-message-mapper.ts translates SDK stream messages into the stable UI contract and into richer product-owned HarnessEvents.

Internal interface EngineConformanceSuite is the test set any engine adapter, including the first SDK adapter, must pass before becoming the production path.

Internal interface EngineAdapter is the provider-specific translator converting external identifiers, message names, permission modes, tool names, transcript paths, and session IDs into provider-neutral Chirality contracts.
Internal interface TurnEngine is the thin owner for a single harness turn lifecycle around SDK query() through the engine contract.
Internal interface SdkOptionsBuilder deterministically constructs SDK options from Chirality session, persona, mode, tool, MCP, hook, permission, and settings-isolation policy.
Internal interface SdkMessageMapper maps SDK messages into browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents.
Internal interface PersonaComposer builds the system prompt / appended prompt from instruction root, active persona, mode, and working-root policy.
Internal interface HarnessEvent is the persisted runtime event.
Internal interface SessionEvents is the append/replay JSONL event API.
Internal interface RunLogger is the redacted structured runtime logger.

Internal interface RelianceBoundaryRegister is the product-owned list of audit, permission, lifecycle, filesystem, transcript, and human-gate semantics with their enforcement surfaces and fallback implications.
Internal interface ChiralityPermissionOverlay implements adapter mode, disallowed tool, hook, explicit hard-deny precedence, and canUseTool policy.

Internal interface ChiralityHooks provides SDK hook callbacks for path containment, instruction-root protection, symlink policy, provenance, failure triage, compaction mirror, and subagent governance.
Internal interface ChiralityMcpTools provides in-process SDK MCP server definitions for deterministic Chirality operations.
Internal interface SdkSessionLink provides metadata and helpers for sdkSessionId, SDK project key, transcript path/store key, and resume behavior.
Internal interface ToolResultStore is the product-owned artifact and preview policy for large or sensitive tool outputs.
Internal interface SubagentGovernanceBridge generates/validates SDK agents definitions and fail-closed Agent tool gating through evaluateSubagentGovernance.

Internal interface DomainEngineProfile is the future-amendment contract describing deterministic domain engine boundaries, protected paths, proposal paths, operations, manifests, and boundary notices.
Internal interface OperationProposal is the future-amendment record for proposed domain operations requiring deterministic checks and human gates before application.

Current runtime implementation truth remains in source, tests, validation artifacts, and git history.
Current coordination state is discovered rather than tracked in a separate next-instance state file.
The document title is RELEASE QUALITY GATES for Chirality App Dev.
RELEASE_QUALITY_GATES is a Draft governance support surface.
The product covered is the Chirality desktop harness and bundled agent operating system.
The gates apply to release-significant app-dev changes, validation evidence, packaging evidence, and release-quality review.
This checklist routes app-dev changes through release-quality evidence gates.
The release quality gates complement docs/VALIDATION_STRATEGY.md, docs/BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md, and the invariants in docs/CONTRACT.md.
The gates define evidence to collect or explicitly waive before a release-significant change is accepted.
The gates do not publish a release, approve lifecycle issuance, certify professional work, seal or authenticate work product, declare code compliance, or authorize external distribution.
Run every release-significant change through all applicable gate families.
Coordination policy, completion plans, decision-register pointers, and docs-only governance changes route to the Governance gate.
Runtime contract, adapter boundary, turn lifecycle, session events, and event schema changes route to the Runtime contract gate.
SDK options, permissions, tools, hooks, MCP, and path policy changes route to the Permission/tool gate.
API routes, harness workflow, running-app validation, attachments, and interrupt behavior changes route to the Harness workflow gate.
Network, API key handling, redaction, and provider policy changes route to the Security and network gate.
UI workflow, product identity, and professional-boundary copy changes route to the UI and claims gate.
Instruction-root resources, Electron build, package metadata, and DMG output changes route to the Packaging gate.
Future domain-engine profiles, adapters, and operation proposals route to the Domain-adapter gate.
Mixed changes run the union of applicable gates unless a human project authority records an explicit waiver and risk disposition.
Every gate record or closeout summary should include the change identifier, scope, affected files, and owner/agent.
Every gate record or closeout summary should include the commands run and their pass/fail results.
Every gate record should include the generated summary artifact path where a command emits one.
Every gate record should include skipped checks and the reason each was skipped.
Every gate record should include known limitations, unresolved TBD items, and human-ruling blockers.
Every gate record should confirm that runtime events, logs, plans, and completion logs are evidence/history only.
Every gate record should confirm the work makes no release-readiness, professional-approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance claim.
The Governance gate is used for docs-only governance, coordination, plan, and decision-register changes.
Governance gate evidence requires git diff --check over affected docs, plans, and coordination paths.
Governance gate evidence requires targeted stale-reference searches for the rule or authority being replaced.
Governance gate evidence requires existence checks for new relative links and referenced local paths.
Governance gate evidence requires confirmation that _DECISIONS/_REGISTER.md remains the decision-tracking table when decision state is not being changed.
Governance gate evidence requires confirmation that no runtime source, package manifest, or wrapper file changed when the tranche is governance-only.
Frontend tests are normally skipped for governance-only tranches and the closeout must say so explicitly.
The Runtime contract gate is used for changes to the runtime engine contract, adapter boundary, turn lifecycle, persisted events, replay behavior, or session storage.
Runtime contract gate evidence requires focused tests for the touched runtime modules.
Runtime contract gate evidence requires running npm run typecheck.
Runtime contract gate evidence requires the broader npm run test when shared event or route behavior changes.
Runtime contract gate evidence requires harness premerge validation when browser-facing session, SSE, or turn behavior changes.
Runtime contract gate evidence requires review that public/core Chirality contracts do not become SDK-shaped except as adapter metadata.
The Permission and tool gate is used for SDK options, permission overlay, tool descriptors, tool exposure, hooks, MCP wrappers, path policy, or tool-result evidence.
Permission and tool gate evidence requires tests for allow, deny, ask, and unknown-tool behavior where applicable.
Permission and tool gate evidence requires tests proving write/edit/bash/network/subagent capabilities remain denied until the active plan and human rulings authorize them.
Permission and tool gate evidence requires running npm run typecheck.
No new model-visible tool exposure is allowed without descriptor, permission, event, and validation coverage.
No path write policy relaxation is allowed without human ruling and tests.
The Harness workflow gate is used for session boot, turn execution, SSE streaming, interrupt/cancel behavior, attachment validation, working-root behavior, and validation scripts.
Harness workflow gate evidence requires relevant API and library tests.
Harness workflow gate evidence requires running npm run harness:validate:premerge against a reachable local harness API.
Harness workflow gate evidence requires review of frontend/artifacts/harness/section8/latest/summary.json when generated.
Harness workflow gate evidence requires preservation of stable browser-facing SSE event names unless a governed compatibility change authorizes them.
The Security and network gate is used for API keys, network policy, provider scope, redaction, stored logs, or outbound request behavior.
Security and network gate evidence requires relevant key-storage, redaction, and network-policy tests.
Security and network gate evidence requires running npm run proof:network-policy when network or provider behavior changes.
Security and network gate evidence requires confirmation that API keys are not written to project files, runtime events, logs, tool artifacts, or SDK transcript imports.

Security and network gate evidence requires confirmation that outbound network remains loopback plus the current shipped Anthropic path unless a bounded future implementation tranche and recorded decision evidence broaden it.
The UI and claims gate is used for product copy, workflow labels, navigation, review states, professional-boundary notices, and user-facing validation or release text.
UI and claims gate evidence requires relevant component or library tests where available.
UI and claims gate evidence requires targeted visual/manual review when layout, labels, or user-facing workflow changes.
No wording may say or imply Chirality approves professional work, proves code compliance, externally validates work, signs, seals, certifies, authenticates, publishes, or issues work for reliance.
UI copy must maintain a clear distinction between draft/proposal/runtime evidence and human-accepted project truth.
The Packaging gate is used for instruction-root resources, Electron build configuration, package metadata, release scripts, DMG output, or distribution artifacts.
Packaging gate evidence requires reviewing the command and artifact posture in docs/BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md.
Packaging gate evidence requires running npm run instruction-root:integrity.
Packaging gate evidence requires running npm run build.
Packaging gate evidence requires running npm run desktop:pack for package-layout changes.
Packaging gate evidence requires running npm run desktop:dist for DMG/distribution changes or release-candidate review.
Packaging gate evidence requires the generated artifact path, checksum when applicable, signing/notarization state, and known limitations.
The current release target remains macOS 15+ Apple Silicon unsigned/unnotarized local-builder DMG unless a governed amendment changes it.
The Domain-adapter gate is used for future domain-engine profiles, protected paths, adapters, operation proposals, deterministic domain checks, or domain-output presentation.
Domain-adapter gate evidence requires a human ruling that the domain-adapter tranche is in scope.
Domain-adapter gate evidence requires proposal-record and human-gate semantics before any protected domain state mutation.
Domain-adapter gate evidence requires path containment and write-quarantine tests where implementation exists.
Domain-adapter gate evidence requires product copy review preserving that domain engines own domain truth and Chirality governs interaction, proposals, records, and human gates.
A waiver must be explicit and must name the waived gate item, reason, affected scope, compensating evidence, known risk, and human decision record.

No waiver may authorize hidden project truth, protected instruction-root writes, private-data exposure, broad network access, unapproved bash/tool exposure, professional-approval claims, or release-publication claims.
An open release-quality decision is the hosted CI provider and workflow location.
An open release-quality decision is the final release matrix, signing, notarization, publication, and attestation.
An open release-quality decision is the release-label vocabulary and release-candidate evidence bundle format.
An open release-quality decision is coverage, performance, and permitted-variance thresholds.
An open release-quality decision is the concrete provider/network implementation beyond the current shipped Anthropic path.
Any attempt to reverse the D-APP-01/D-APP-02 Pi pattern-corpus-only ruling remains an open decision.

UnitStatement: This document is the authoritative specification for Chirality App physical structures, file formats, schemas, runtime mechanics, session storage, validation surfaces, and layout conventions.
Normative keywords MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are used in their ordinary specification sense.
The instruction root is the release-managed resource set bundled with the desktop app or supplied through CHIRALITY_INSTRUCTION_ROOT during development.

A complete source tree or packaged app instruction root requires entries including AGENTS.md, README.md, agents/, docs/, docs/DIRECTIVE.md, docs/CONTRACT.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/TYPES.md, and docs/PLAN.md.
docs/WHAT-IS-AN-AGENT.md and PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md are required instruction-root entries where required by packaging/integrity policy.
The instruction root is read-only during ordinary project execution.
Writes to the instruction root MUST be blocked by runtime hooks and path policy.
Packaged builds MUST verify instruction-root integrity.
Missing required instruction-root assets are a P0 packaging and runtime-readiness blocker.
The working root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local project folder.
The working root MUST be an absolute existing directory.
The working root MUST be readable and writable by the app.
The working root MUST NOT be inside the instruction root.
The working root contains project execution state, deliverables, tool roots, sessions, and local artifacts.
The working root is the ordinary location where agents and tools write project truth.

Runtime configuration state such as UI presets, API keys, provider/SDK linkage, adapter transcript cross-references, session metadata, and window layout is non-authoritative convenience state unless imported into a governed project file.
An execution instance is rooted at {EXECUTION_ROOT}/ and contains package folders plus tool roots.

The execution root layout includes INIT.md, package folders PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}/, and tool-root folders such as _Aggregation/, _Change/, _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
Package folders are named {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}/.
Package folders MUST include the 1_Working/ subfolder for active deliverables.
Package folders SHOULD include 0_References/ and 0_References/_Archive/ for package-level and archived references.
Package folders SHOULD include 1_Working/_Archive/, 2_Checking/ with From/ and To/, and 3_Issued/ with _Archive/.
Tool roots include _Aggregation/ for aggregation snapshots and templates and _Change/ for change-management records.
Tool roots include _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/ for baseline snapshots with checksums, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
Snapshot-producing workflows SHOULD write timestamped immutable folders and MAY update _LATEST.md pointer files.
Each deliverable occupies {EXECUTION_ROOT}/{PKG-ID}_{PkgLabel}/1_Working/{DEL-ID}_{DelLabel}/.

A deliverable MUST contain _STATUS.md (lifecycle state and history), _CONTEXT.md (identity, package, decomposition reference, traceability), _DEPENDENCIES.md (dependency summary and run history), and _REFERENCES.md (source references and hash notes).
A deliverable SHOULD contain _SEMANTIC.md for the PREPARATION baseline as a semantic placeholder or lens.
When initialized, a deliverable SHOULD contain Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
Dependencies.csv SHOULD be present when tracked as a structured dependency register v3.1.
MEMORY.md SHOULD be present as the canonical deliverable-local working memory.
_MEMORY.md MUST NOT exist in this project profile; it is a disabled noncanonical memory file.
The minimum PREPARATION fileset is _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, and a _SEMANTIC.md placeholder.
The document kit consists of Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
_STATUS.md uses a defined markdown format with a status heading, Current State, Last Updated, and a History section.
The valid _STATUS.md state progression is OPEN -> INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> CHECKING -> ISSUED.
State OPEN means the folder exists with the minimum viable fileset; INITIALIZED means draft documents or document kit initialized.
State SEMANTIC_READY means a semantic lens or placeholder is generated; IN_PROGRESS means human/agent work is underway.
State CHECKING means under human review; ISSUED means released/issued by a human.
Transition to OPEN is authorized by PREPARATION/scaffold; OPEN to INITIALIZED by 4_DOCUMENTS or human.
INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY is authorized by CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK or human; INITIALIZED or SEMANTIC_READY to IN_PROGRESS by human or WORKING_ITEMS.
IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING and CHECKING to ISSUED are authorized by a human.
_STATUS.md is the canonical lifecycle file.
_STATUS.md transitions are forward-only unless a human explicitly amends the record.
Transitions to CHECKING or ISSUED require approval SHA evidence.
SDK/MCP status-transition tools MUST enforce the lifecycle transition rules.
_CONTEXT.md has a required structure including Name, Package, Discipline, Type, Responsible, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Anticipated Artifacts, Scope Traceability, and Decomposition Reference.
_CONTEXT.md header fields SHOULD match the accepted decomposition.
_CONTEXT.md is created by PREPARATION/scaffold and is human-maintained thereafter.

_DEPENDENCIES.md is a hybrid container with human-owned and agent/tool-owned sections: Dependency Tracking Mode, Declared Upstream, Declared Downstream, Extracted Dependency Register, Lifecycle Summary, Run Notes, and Run History.
Dependency tracking mode NOT_TRACKED means dependencies are coordinated externally by humans.
Dependency tracking mode DECLARED means human-declared upstream/downstream only.
Dependency tracking mode TRACKED means full extraction via dependency workflow and Dependencies.csv.
_REFERENCES.md has a required structure with Applicable References (RefName/ID, Location, Relevance, ContentHash) and Notes.
_REFERENCES.md ContentHash is a 64-char lowercase SHA-256, or TBD, or an ERROR with reason.
Reference paths SHOULD be relative where practical.
Out-of-folder references SHOULD include ContentHash when tooling is available.
Hash bypasses require human approval and durable bypass records.
MEMORY.md is the canonical deliverable-local working memory file organized by semantic topic then chronologically.
MEMORY.md sections include Key Decisions & Human Rulings, Domain Context, Open Items, Proposal History, and Interface & Dependency Notes.
_MEMORY.md MUST NOT be created in this project profile.
Every Dependencies.csv row MUST include RegisterSchemaVersion set to v3.1.
Dependencies.csv MUST include RegisterSchemaVersion (v3.1), DependencyID unique within the register, FromPackageID, FromDeliverableID, and FromDeliverableName.
DependencyClass MUST be ANCHOR or EXECUTION; Direction MUST be UPSTREAM or DOWNSTREAM.
AnchorType, DependencyType, and TargetType are MUST enum columns defined in TYPES.
Optional target columns include TargetPackageID, TargetDeliverableID, TargetRefID, and TargetLocation; TargetName SHOULD be a human-readable target.
EvidenceFile and SourceRef are conditionally required columns holding source filename and path-plus-heading, or 'location TBD'.
EvidenceQuote SHOULD be a short quote of no more than 30 words; Explicitness SHOULD be EXPLICIT or IMPLICIT.
SatisfactionStatus SHOULD record closure status; Confidence SHOULD be HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
Origin MUST be DECLARED or EXTRACTED; FirstSeen and LastSeen MUST be ISO dates; Status MUST be ACTIVE or RETIRED.
Extension columns MAY be present and are non-breaking, including EstimateImpactClass and ConsumerHint.
DependencyID MUST be unique within a deliverable register.
FromDeliverableID MUST match the host deliverable ID.
ANCHOR rows use IMPLEMENTS_NODE or TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT with DependencyType=OTHER.
EXECUTION rows use AnchorType=NOT_APPLICABLE.
Dependency rows are retired, not deleted.
Legacy missing RegisterSchemaVersion is normalized on write to v3.1.
Agent instruction files use AGENT_*.md names.
Agent instruction files require a header with [[DOC:AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS]], an AGENT INSTRUCTIONS title, and AGENT_TYPE set to 0, 1, or 2.

The required Agent Type table includes AGENT_TYPE, AGENT_CLASS (PERSONA or TASK), INTERACTION_SURFACE (chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, or both), WRITE_SCOPE, BLOCKING (never or allowed), and PRIMARY_OUTPUTS.
Agent instruction files require section markers PROTOCOL, SPEC, STRUCTURE, and RATIONALE delimited by [[BEGIN:X]] and [[END:X]].
Agent instruction section precedence is PROTOCOL > SPEC > STRUCTURE > RATIONALE.
Machine-consumed YAML frontmatter MAY include description, subagents, tools, model, max_turns, disallowed_tools, and auto_approve_tools.
Runtime MUST treat UI visibility of an option as non-authoritative; governance and permission policy remain authoritative.
Legacy sessions may exist as {sessionRoot}/{sessionId}.json.
Current legacy session fields include sessionId, projectRoot, persona, mode, createdAt, updatedAt, engineSessionId, claudeSessionId, bootFingerprint, bootedAt, and model.
Legacy session records MUST remain readable during migration.
The canonical vNext session layout is .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/ containing session.json, events.jsonl, turns/<turnId>.json, artifacts/, and sdk/.
CHIRALITY_SESSION_ROOT is an optional override for the session root.
session.json SHOULD include sessionId, projectRoot, persona, mode, createdAt, updatedAt, model, bootFingerprint, and engineSessionId.

session.json SHOULD include SDK linkage fields sdkSessionId, sdkProjectKey, sdkTranscriptPath or sdkSessionStoreKey, sdkConfigDir, sdkSettingSources, sdkPackageVersion, sdkClaudeCodeVersion, and sdkResumeMode.
events.jsonl is the product-owned Chirality audit mirror.
SDK transcripts are secondary runtime state unless imported into HarnessEvent form.
The product SHOULD prefer SDK transcript placement or mirroring under the working root or parent project-controlled folder using SessionStore, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or both when reliable.
If the SDK writes under ~/.claude/projects/..., Chirality MUST cross-reference the path or store key, keep events.jsonl canonical, and record residual risk in the reliance-boundary register.
HarnessEvent has fields schemaVersion (1), eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and data as a record.
JSONL writes MUST append newline-delimited events in write sequence.
Event IDs MUST be unique.
Secrets MUST NOT be stored in events.
Large payloads MUST be stored as artifacts and referenced by path.
Replay MUST ignore malformed trailing lines and surface diagnostics.
Event schema evolution MUST be backward-compatible or explicitly versioned.

Initial event categories include session.created, session.resumed, turn.accepted, turn.started, adapter.initialized, model.request.started, model.delta, model.completed, turn.completed, turn.failed, and turn.cancelled.

Later event categories include tool.queued, tool.permission, tool.started, tool.progress, tool.completed, tool.failed, hook.started, hook.completed, context.compacted, subagent.started, subagent.completed, and runtime.mirror.error.
Chirality MUST define an AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract separate from provider/SDK APIs.

The runtime engine's target responsibilities include accepting validated turn input, persisting turn.accepted before adapter/model execution, yielding browser UIEvents, and persisting canonical HarnessEvents.

The runtime engine's target responsibilities include enforcing or invoking permission decisions, exposing only permitted tools, linking adapter session metadata, handling interrupt/cancel behavior, and persisting terminal outcomes.
AgentEnginePort defines runTurn(input: TurnInput) returning AsyncIterable<UIEvent> and an optional interrupt(sessionId) returning Promise<void>.
TurnInput MUST include the active session, normalized project root, persona, mode, resolved runtime options, content blocks, attachment summaries, and cancellation signal where applicable.
Provider/SDK messages are not the browser contract and not the canonical persisted event contract.
Provider/SDK-specific names and IDs appear only as adapter metadata.
EngineAdapter MUST translate external message names, session IDs, tool names, permission modes, transcript paths, and hook names into Chirality-owned contracts.
Provider-specific values MAY be retained under explicit adapter metadata fields.
Any provider/SDK-backed adapter MUST pass engine conformance tests before production default use.
The current Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic adapter is the first concrete adapter and current shipped path.
A stub adapter remains available for deterministic tests.
/api/harness/turn remains a transport adapter that validates request shape, obtains session lock, forwards input to TurnEngine, writes SSE, and handles cleanup, and does not own runtime policy.
Turn streams emit named SSE events with JSON payloads: session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit.
Existing SSE event names MUST remain compatible during SDK adoption.
Additional tool progress events MAY be introduced only with UI compatibility handling.
The stream MUST terminate with a process-level completion/error signal unless the client disconnects.
Client disconnect cleanup MUST record cancellation once the event log exists.

Chirality uses a provider-adapter runtime architecture with Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic as the first concrete adapter and current shipped path, subject to R0/R1 empirical verification and ongoing conformance tests.
Concrete non-Anthropic providers require bounded future implementation scope.
Shipped builds MUST use settingSources: [].
Development-only project settings MAY use ['project'] behind explicit environment configuration.
User and local setting sources MUST NOT be used in shipped builds.
API key precedence is UI safeStorage key first, then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then CHIRALITY_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Key material is supplied to the provider/SDK environment only as needed for active turns and redacted from logs/events.

Safe adapter runtime metadata SHOULD include provider/SDK package version, Claude Code subprocess version where knowable, provider/SDK permission mode, visible tool list, MCP server names, settings-source posture, provider/SDK session ID and resume mode, and transcript/store linkage.
Model fallback chain is opts.model -> CHIRALITY_GLOBAL_MODEL or instruction-root frontmatter -> runtime default.
Tools fallback chain is opts.tools -> persona frontmatter -> runtime default; max turns is opts.maxTurns -> persona frontmatter -> runtime default.
Mode fallback is request/session mode -> runtime default; persona fallback is request/session persona -> HELP_HUMAN or configured default.
Unknown option keys MUST be ignored with warnings rather than silently mutating behavior.

The persona composer builds the system prompt from the Chirality governance preface, selected agents/AGENT_<persona>.md content, working-root summary, mode policy, permitted tool surface, and professional-boundary reminders.

Boot fingerprints SHOULD include hashes for persona content, governance preface, mode, adapter tool names/versions, permission-policy version, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version.
First-adapter SDK built-ins map to SDK names: Read for read file, LS/Glob for list files, Grep for search, Write for write file, Edit for edit file, and Bash for shell command.
Chirality-specific deterministic operations use mcp__chirality__* names.
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__status_read (read _STATUS.md) and mcp__chirality__status_transition (apply authorized lifecycle transition with approval SHA, write-gated).
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__deps_read (read and validate Dependencies.csv) and mcp__chirality__deps_write (append/update dependency rows preserving v3.1 schema, write-gated).
Initial Chirality MCP tools include mcp__chirality__scope_scan (bounded workspace scope scan, read) and mcp__chirality__scaffold (wrap scaffold service or dry-run preview, gated).
Unknown opts.tools names MUST produce structured validation errors.
Tool ordering MUST be deterministic.
Denied tools SHOULD be omitted from model context where possible.
allowedTools MUST NOT be treated as a restriction boundary by itself.
Explicit hard-deny precedence, disallowedTools, permissionMode, canUseTool, and hooks enforce restrictions.
Chirality readOnly mode prefers SDK plan or dontAsk with read tools pre-approved and denies write/edit/bash/network-capable and unexpected tools.
Chirality workspaceWrite mode uses SDK acceptEdits only after write hooks pass and enforces project-root containment, instruction-root block, symlink rejection, and provenance.
Chirality dontAsk mode uses SDK dontAsk or an equivalent deny-without-prompt overlay, pre-approving exact safe tools while everything else denies without prompting.
Chirality ask mode uses SDK default with canUseTool, presenting UI approval for governed writes/shell and persisting the decision before returning SDK allow/deny.
Chirality bypass mode uses SDK bypassPermissions only in developer-local mode and still applies hard-deny rules, disallowed tools, path hooks, instruction-root protection, and subagent governance.
Required hooks include path containment (deny filesystem operations outside the active project root) and instruction-root protection (deny writes under the instruction root).
Required hooks include symlink write rejection, write budget enforcement, and provenance append where policy requires.
Required hooks include PreCompact mirror (persist compaction boundary), Stop/finalization (persist terminal outcome), and subagent governance (gate the Agent tool through evaluateSubagentGovernance).
Hook failures fail closed for write, shell, domain, and subagent actions.
Supported attachment extensions are .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .pdf, .txt, .md, and .csv.

The server-side attachment resolver MUST enforce path validation, regular-file check, symlink rejection, extension allowlist, readability, a per-file 10 MB limit, and a total raw-byte 18 MB per-turn limit.
Partial attachment failure is non-fatal when executable content remains; if all attachments fail and user text is empty the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE.
The API key store uses Electron storage at app.getPath('userData')/credentials/api-key.enc.
API key store rules: use Electron safeStorage, do not write key material to working root, do not log key material, and do not persist key material in runtime events.
API key status may report source as ui, env, or none.
Renderer outbound traffic is allowlisted for loopback and the current shipped Anthropic API path.
Node/provider/SDK calls must not silently broaden network policy.
Provider-adapter generality is approved strategically, but concrete non-Anthropic providers, remote MCP, plugins, and network-capable tools require bounded governed future implementation scope.
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/session/create (create session bound to projectRoot, persona, mode) and POST /api/harness/session/boot (boot session and persist boot metadata).
Harness APIs include GET /api/harness/session/list (list sessions for normalized project root) and GET/DELETE /api/harness/session/[id] (retrieve or delete session).
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/turn (execute turn and stream UI events over SSE) and POST /api/harness/interrupt (interrupt active turn).
Harness APIs include POST /api/harness/scaffold (scaffold execution root from decomposition markdown).
Existing harness route shapes remain stable during adapter adoption and TurnEngine extraction.
Workspace APIs include POST /api/working-root/validate, GET /api/working-root/tree (bounded file tree), and GET /api/working-root/scope (scan deliverables and knowledge types).
Workspace APIs include GET /api/project/deliverables (deliverables plus knowledge decomposition metadata) and GET /api/working-root/deliverable/status (read _STATUS.md snapshot).
Workspace APIs include POST /api/working-root/deliverable/status/transition (apply allowed lifecycle transition) and GET/PUT /api/working-root/deliverable/dependencies (read/write Dependencies.csv).

Domain-engine endpoints and tools are provisional future platform interfaces that must not be implemented as current-release scope and must not imply automated professional acceptance or direct protected-model writes.

Candidate domain endpoint families include /api/domain/profiles/list, /api/domain/profiles/validate, /api/domain/artifacts/scan, /api/domain/operations/propose, /api/domain/operations/validate, and /api/domain/operations/apply.
Future domain profiles MUST define protected paths, proposal paths, operations, artifact types, deterministic adapter manifests, and boundary notices.
Applying a domain operation requires explicit human acceptance.
Required local checks from frontend/ are npm run test, npm run typecheck, npm run harness:validate:premerge, and npm run instruction-root:integrity.
Packaging uses npm run desktop:dist.
Expected packaging outputs are frontend/dist/Chirality-0.1.0-arm64.dmg, frontend/dist/mac-arm64/Chirality.app, and frontend/artifacts/harness/instruction-root-integrity/latest/summary.json.
Notes: frontend/ path references; known publish-time drift per project memory

UnitStatement: Section 8 validation verifies server reachable, session CRUD, boot error taxonomy, smoke stream ordering, session persistence and resume continuity, permissions behavior, interrupt behavior, and SDK-native stream handling with no legacy parser regressions.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs to add as phases land include section9.runtime_engine_contract, section9.adapter_turn_engine_event_log, section9.adapter_message_mapper, and section9.session_event_replay.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs include section9.reliance_boundary_register, section9.settingsources_isolation, section9.sdk_session_link_resume, and section9.permission_overlay_hard_deny_precedence.

Section 9 runtime validation IDs include section9.tool_runtime_read_file, section9.chirality_mcp_status_dependencies, section9.path_containment_hook, section9.instruction_root_protection_hook, section9.tool_result_budget, section9.context_compaction_boundary, section9.subagent_governance_hook, and section9.domain_profile_validation.
Manual macOS DMG release verification checks that the binary is arm64, LSMinimumSystemVersion is 15.0.0 or later, and signing posture is unsigned/adhoc as scoped.

Manual release verification checks that app resources contain required instruction-root assets, the working-root selector is available, and current loopback plus Anthropic network guardrails remain in force.

Manual release verification checks that a first-adapter SDK-backed turn can start in the packaged app after R1, the SDK subprocess/binary is executable from package layout, and SDK transcript storage/mirroring follows the accepted R1 decision.
Sanitize(name) replaces /, \, :, *, ?, double-quote, <, >, and | with a hyphen.
Sanitize(name) collapses consecutive whitespace to one space and trims leading/trailing whitespace.
Folder names are Package {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)} and Deliverable {DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}.
Canonical unsanitized names are stored in _CONTEXT.md and decomposition records.
TYPES.md is the authoritative vocabulary reference for Chirality App, defining canonical entities, stable identifier formats, enumerated values, agent roles, runtime vocabulary, and type targets.
Where a term is used differently elsewhere, this document governs unless a higher-authority source has been explicitly amended.
The project hierarchy is flat: {EXECUTION_ROOT}/PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}/1_Working/DEL-XX-YY_{DelLabel}/.
A Package is a flat partition of project scope; packages do not nest.
Each package contains references, active working deliverables, checking staging, and issued artifacts.
A Deliverable is a unit of production within a package.
Each deliverable has a stable ID, lifecycle state, context file, dependency record, reference record, and optional document kit or specialized artifacts.
An Artifact is a tangible output such as a markdown document, CSV register, tool-root snapshot, domain proposal, runtime event file, or validation summary.
Artifacts are authoritative only when placed in the proper project location and accepted by the relevant process.
A Tool Root is a project-level directory for derived outputs such as _Aggregation/, _Change/, _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
The Instruction Root is the release-managed app resource tree containing governance documents, agent instructions, and framework materials; ordinary project execution must not mutate it.
The Working Root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local filesystem location where project execution state, sessions, artifacts, and git history live.
Project Truth is gate-relevant project state represented in versioned project files.
Runtime transcripts, chat drafts, UI state, API keys, SDK transcripts, and caches are not project truth unless a governed process imports relevant content into project files.

The Runtime Audit Mirror is the product-owned runtime event log, normally .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl, used to reconstruct and review accepted turns, model output, permissions, tool activity, hooks, compaction boundaries, and subagent lifecycle.
Identifiers are assigned once and persist across renames and path changes.
Package ID format is PKG-XX or PKG-XXX (e.g., PKG-01), assigned by Decomposition / human approval.
Deliverable ID format is DEL-XX-YY or DEL-XXX-YY (e.g., DEL-01-01), assigned by Decomposition / human approval.
Dependency ID format is DEP-XX-YY-NNN (e.g., DEP-01-01-001), assigned by the DEPENDENCIES workflow/tool.
Scope Item ID format is SOW-NNN (e.g., SOW-003), assigned by Decomposition.
Objective ID format is OBJ-NNN (e.g., OBJ-001), assigned by Decomposition.
Session ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., sess_...), assigned by the Harness session manager.
Turn ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., turn_...), assigned by TurnEngine.
Runtime Event ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., evt_...), assigned by SessionEvents.
Subagent Run ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., subrun_...), assigned by SubagentGovernanceBridge.
Domain Profile ID is a domain-profile-id string (e.g., openpipestress), assigned by a future domain profile author.
Operation Proposal ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., op_...), assigned by a future domain operation workflow.
Folder names combine stable ID and sanitized label: Package as {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}; Deliverable as {DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}.
The unsanitized canonical name belongs in _CONTEXT.md or the governing decomposition document.
XX, YY, and NNN are zero-padded numeric sequences.
Deliverable IDs use hyphen separators, not dots.
Stable IDs must not change unless a human explicitly approves renumbering.
Runtime event IDs are unique per event and never reused.
Type 0 (Architect) defines and maintains rules, standards, contracts, and role boundaries; scope is project-wide or system-wide.
Type 1 (Manager) interprets intent, decomposes work, routes specialists, and reconciles outputs; scope is project, package, or workflow.
Type 2 (Specialist) executes bounded briefs with minimal context and returns outputs plus evidence; scope is deliverable-local or narrow task.
AGENT_CLASS has values PERSONA and TASK: persona agents run interactive sessions; task agents run straight-through or delegated work.
INTERACTION_SURFACE has values chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, both, indicating how the agent is invoked.
WRITE_SCOPE has values repo-wide, project-level, deliverable-local, tool-root-only, workspace-scaffold-only, repo-metadata-only, none, indicating permitted write area.
BLOCKING has values never and allowed, indicating whether the agent may pause for human input.
Authority flows downward; escalation flows upward.
Type 0 defines what correct means; Type 1 prepares, routes, and reconciles work; Type 2 executes bounded work.
Humans approve, issue, sign, seal, and accept reliance.
A Type 2 agent cannot modify Type 0 rules; a Type 1 agent cannot issue work for reliance; no agent can approve professional work.
Persona alias HELP maps to canonical agent HELP_HUMAN.
Persona alias ORCHESTRATE maps to canonical agent ORCHESTRATOR.
Persona alias AGGREGATE maps to canonical agent AGGREGATION.
Persona alias RECONCILING maps to canonical agent RECONCILIATION.
Persona alias AGENTS maps to canonical agent HELPS_HUMANS.
Matrix row NORMATIVE covers guidance, orchestration, standards, and aggregation support; destination WORKBENCH.
Matrix row OPERATIVE covers pipeline execution categories; destination PIPELINE.
Matrix row EVALUATIVE covers review, dependencies, change, and reconciliation support; destination WORKBENCH.
Matrix column GUIDING helps orient or define the work.
Matrix column APPLYING helps execute or apply the work.
Matrix column JUDGING helps inspect, assess, or manage work items.
Matrix column REVIEWING helps aggregate, reconcile, or review work.
NORMATIVE row cells: Guiding=HELP, Applying=ORCHESTRATE, Judging=WORKING_ITEMS, Reviewing=AGGREGATE.
OPERATIVE row cells: Guiding=DECOMP*, Applying=PREP*, Judging=TASK*, Reviewing=AUDIT*.
EVALUATIVE row cells: Guiding=AGENTS, Applying=DEPENDENCIES, Judging=CHANGE, Reviewing=RECONCILING.
PipelineCategory has values DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, AUDIT*, the top-level operative category.
TaskScopeMode has values DELIVERABLES and KNOWLEDGE_TYPES, the dynamic scope mode for TASK*.
KnowledgeTypeOption values are Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, Procedure, Dependencies, References, Context, Status, Semantic, Memory; file-type buckets discovered from deliverable content.
DisabledOption is any visible but non-selectable option, a coming-soon or unsupported variant intentionally shown without enabling runtime selection.
Deliverable lifecycle states are tracked in _STATUS.md.
The deliverable lifecycle sequence is OPEN -> INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> CHECKING -> ISSUED.
OPEN means the folder exists with minimum viable fileset; content is not yet initialized.
INITIALIZED means the document kit has been drafted or initialized.
SEMANTIC_READY means a semantic lens or semantic placeholder has been generated.
IN_PROGRESS means active human and/or agent work is underway.
CHECKING means work is under human review.
ISSUED means work has been released/issued by a human.
Stage gates such as 30%, 60%, 90%, or IFC are project milestones, not lifecycle states.

The INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY transition is optional; if semantic lensing is skipped, deliverables may transition directly from INITIALIZED -> IN_PROGRESS under the authorized actor rules in SPEC.md.
Dependency class ANCHOR connects a deliverable to a definition or traceability node; graph role is tree edge.
Dependency class EXECUTION captures information flow, prerequisite, handoff, interface, or constraint; graph role is DAG edge.
Anchor type IMPLEMENTS_NODE is the parent definition node, normally one per deliverable.
Anchor type TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT is a requirement trace link, zero or more per deliverable.
Anchor type NOT_APPLICABLE is used for execution rows.
Direction UPSTREAM means the host deliverable requires information from the target.
Direction DOWNSTREAM means the host deliverable produces information for the target.
Legacy INBOUND normalizes to UPSTREAM; legacy OUTBOUND normalizes to DOWNSTREAM.
Dependency type PREREQUISITE is a required input or approval before work can proceed.
Dependency type INTERFACE is an explicit data or artifact exchange.
Dependency type HANDOVER is output consumed as input by another work item.
Dependency type CONSTRAINT is an explicit constraint or condition.
Dependency type ENABLES means the host deliverable enables downstream work.
Dependency type OTHER is a catch-all and is required for anchor rows.
Legacy COORDINATION and INFORMATION dependency types are not emitted in new extractions.
Target type DELIVERABLE is another deliverable in the project.
Target type PACKAGE is a package.
Target type WBS_NODE is a work breakdown or scope node.
Target type REQUIREMENT is a requirement, SOW item, objective, or acceptance item.
Target type DOCUMENT is an external or reference document.
Target type EQUIPMENT is physical equipment or asset.
Target type EXTERNAL is an external entity, organization, code, standard, or interface.
Target type UNKNOWN means the target cannot be confidently resolved.
Explicitness has values EXPLICIT and IMPLICIT, indicating whether the dependency is directly stated.
Confidence has values HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, indicating strength of evidence.
Origin has values DECLARED and EXTRACTED, distinguishing human-declared versus agent/tool-extracted dependencies.
SatisfactionStatus has values TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, NOT_APPLICABLE, the closure lifecycle.
Status has values ACTIVE and RETIRED, the extraction lifecycle.
AgentEnginePort is the product-owned boundary for running a turn, yielding UI events, recording canonical events, enforcing permissions, managing session linkage, and terminal outcomes.
RuntimeEngineContract is the formal expectations an engine adapter must satisfy before use.
EngineAdapter is a provider/SDK-specific implementation behind AgentEnginePort that translates provider-specific events, sessions, permissions, and tool names into Chirality-owned contracts.
ProviderAdapter is the concrete integration layer for an external agent provider or provider SDK.
FirstAdapter is the current concrete Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic adapter path; it is the first shipped path, not the strategic ceiling.
EngineConformanceSuite is the tests proving an adapter satisfies Chirality contracts.
TurnEngine is the runtime service that owns a single turn lifecycle and invokes the engine through the product-owned boundary.
SdkOptionsBuilder is the deterministic constructor for first-adapter SDK options from Chirality state and policy.
SdkMessageMapper is the first-adapter mapper from SDK stream messages into browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents.
PersonaComposer is the builder for system prompt / appended prompt from instruction root, active persona, mode, and working-root policy.
RelianceBoundaryRegister is the record of product-critical semantics and their enforcement surfaces.

PiPatternCorpus is a reference corpus for stable agentic patterns observed in Pi packages and behavior; it is not a runtime dependency, adapter target, fork target, package import path, or spike authorization.
SessionRecord is a metadata record for a harness session.
sessionId is the Chirality session identifier.
engineSessionId is the provider-neutral adapter session identifier exposed by the runtime boundary when available.
sdkSessionId is the SDK session identifier used for resume; it is adapter metadata, not Chirality identity.
sdkProjectKey is the SDK project key or encoded cwd, if exposed.
sdkTranscriptPath is the path to the SDK transcript when applicable; secondary to Chirality audit events.
sdkSessionStoreKey is the key used by a configured SDK session store or mirror.
sdkConfigDir is the explicit SDK config directory when redirected to project-controlled storage.
events.jsonl is the append-only Chirality runtime audit mirror.
session.json is the session metadata/index file.
artifacts/ is the session-local artifact folder for large tool outputs and child-run outputs.
The HarnessEvent type target has fields schemaVersion:1, eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and data (Record<string, unknown>).

Initial HarnessEvent categories are session.created, session.resumed, turn.accepted, turn.started, adapter.initialized, model.request.started, model.delta, model.completed, turn.completed, turn.failed, turn.cancelled.

Later HarnessEvent categories are tool.queued, tool.permission, tool.started, tool.progress, tool.completed, tool.failed, hook.started, hook.completed, context.compacted, subagent.started, subagent.completed, runtime.mirror.error.
Browser-facing turn streams use compact UI events; provider/SDK messages are not the UI contract.
Browser UIEvent SSE event names are session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, process:exit.
Permission mode readOnly allows read-only tools only; write/edit/bash/network-capable tools are denied.
Permission mode workspaceWrite allows governed writes inside project root after hooks and policy pass.
Permission mode dontAsk denies unapproved actions rather than prompting.
Permission mode ask means the application may request interactive approval for governed actions.
Permission mode bypass is a developer-local escape hatch only, never shipped as ordinary mode, and still subject to explicit Chirality hard denies.
Capability policy is the Chirality-owned policy that decides which tools and capabilities are exposed and executable for a session, persona, mode, provider adapter, and validation state.
Explicit hard-deny precedence overrides allows at reliance boundaries, secrets, protected paths, release/professional claims, destructive actions, and unvalidated provider/network expansion.
The HarnessPermissionDecision type target has fields decisionId, sessionId, optional turnId, toolName, decision (allow|deny|ask), reason, source, decidedAt, and optional safeMetadata.
HarnessPermissionDecision source values are sdk-option, sdk-callback, chirality-policy, hook, human, prompt-support.
ask is an application-level state; SDK callbacks ultimately return an allow or deny decision.
SDK built-in tool is a tool supplied by the current first-adapter SDK, such as Read, Glob, Grep, LS, Write, Edit, or Bash where available.
Chirality MCP tool is an in-process deterministic Chirality operation exposed through SDK MCP tooling with mcp__chirality__* naming.
allowedTools is an SDK option that may auto-approve tools; not by itself a restriction boundary.
disallowedTools is an SDK option or Chirality wrapper policy used to prevent tool use or remove tools from context; participates in explicit hard-deny precedence.
canUseTool is an SDK callback or equivalent hook path used by Chirality to mediate permission decisions.
ToolResultStore is the Chirality artifact and preview policy for tool outputs.

Initial in-process MCP tool names are mcp__chirality__status_read, mcp__chirality__status_transition, mcp__chirality__deps_read, mcp__chirality__deps_write, mcp__chirality__scope_scan, mcp__chirality__scaffold.
Future domain tools use mcp__chirality__domain_* only after a governed domain-profile amendment.
Hook PreToolUse runs before tool execution and can deny write/shell/domain/subagent actions.
Hook PostToolUse runs after successful tool execution and may record provenance, budgets, and summaries.
Hook PostToolUseFailure runs after tool failure and records triage and safe diagnostics.
Hook PreCompact records the compaction boundary before SDK/model context compaction where available.
Hook Stop finalizes the terminal turn event.
Hooks SubagentStart / SubagentStop record governed child-run lifecycle where supported.
Claude Agent SDK is the current first concrete hosted runtime substrate for generic agent-loop mechanics; an implementation substrate, not product identity or strategic ceiling.
SDK transcript is the SDK-managed session transcript, secondary to the Chirality audit mirror.
settingSources is an SDK option controlling filesystem settings load; shipped builds use [].
SessionStore is the SDK session mirror/storage mechanism when used; mirror reliability is not assumed to be canonical.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is an environment mechanism that may redirect SDK local config/transcript behavior if empirically reliable.
permissionMode is an SDK permission posture translated from Chirality mode plus capability policy and explicit hard-deny precedence.
bypassPermissions is an SDK mode not permitted in shipped ordinary workflows.
Pi pattern corpus is a reference source for agentic patterns only; D-APP-01 and D-APP-02 rule out Pi adapter, fork, package import, Node 22 sidecar, runtime-floor migration, and immediate spike work.
SDK terms belong at the adapter boundary; public Chirality APIs and canonical events use Chirality terms.

The ChildRunRecord type target has fields contractVersion:1, childRunId, parentSessionId, optional parentTurnId, parentPersona, agentName, projectRoot, mode, status, capabilityPolicy, governance, optional outputArtifactPath, and optional adapter.
ChildRunRecord status values are queued, denied, running, completed, failed, cancelled.
ChildRunRecord capabilityPolicy has inheritParentCapabilities:false, requestedToolNames, allowedToolNames, and deniedCapabilities.
ChildRunRecord governance has state (allowed|denied|adapter-observed), optional gate, optional reason, optional approvalRef, optional approvedBy, allowlistedSubagents, and delegatedSubagents.
ChildRunRecord adapter has adapterName plus optional adapterSessionId, adapterAgentId, adapterTaskId, adapterToolUseId, and adapterTranscriptKey.
evaluateSubagentGovernance is the authoritative fail-closed gate for delegation.
A Type 2 candidate is an agent instruction with AGENT_TYPE: 2 and preferred AGENT_CLASS: TASK.
Parent session is the session requesting delegation.
Child run is the governed subagent execution record.
Context sealed is the required governance condition confirming bounded context.
Pipeline run approved is the required governance condition for Type 2 task invocation.
Approval reference is a non-empty human/gate evidence string required before delegation.

The DomainEngineProfile interface has fields profileId, engineName, optional engineVersion, protectedPaths, proposalPaths, artifactTypes, operations (DomainEngineOperationDescriptor[]), manifestRules, and boundaryNotice.

The OperationProposal interface has fields proposalId, profileId, operationName, createdAt, createdBy, inputRefs, intendedChanges, deterministicChecks, expectedOutputRefs, risks, requiredHumanGate, and status.
OperationProposal status values are draft, ready_for_review, accepted, rejected, applied.
Protected path is an authoritative domain-engine artifact path not directly writable by agents.
Proposal path is an agent-writable folder for proposed changes, summaries, or review aids.
Deterministic adapter is a tool/bridge that validates or applies domain operations under profile rules.
Boundary notice is required copy explaining that Chirality does not approve, validate, or own solver truth.
OpenPipeStress fixture is a potential first domain profile fixture, not Chirality core.
Section 8 validation is the existing harness validation surface for baseline behavior.
Section 9 validation is new runtime validation IDs added as vNext phases land.
instruction-root:integrity is a packaging check verifying required instruction-root resources.
desktop:dist is the desktop build target producing a macOS arm64 DMG.
harness:validate:premerge is the premerge harness validation script producing a stable summary artifact.
settingsources_isolation validates that shipped SDK options do not load ambient user/local settings.
runtime_engine_contract validates that the engine adapter satisfies the product-owned contract.
sdk_session_link_resume validates that SDK session ID/linkage persists and resumes through Chirality metadata.
Priority P0 is required for current release usefulness, safety, or runtime foundation.
Priority P1 is important for quality, governed operation, or runtime maturity.
Priority P2 is later hardening, future extension, or desirable capability.

The framework separates how teams coordinate from how the system tracks dependencies; deliverable-local registers remain the dependency tracking substrate while _COORDINATION.md records the project coordination representation.
Coordination representation SCHEDULE_FIRST means Gantt or schedule logic drives sequencing while dependency tracking remains active for blocker detection and audit.
Coordination representation DEPENDENCY_TRACKED means dependency graph logic drives sequencing and handoff analysis.
Coordination representation HYBRID means schedule-first and dependency-tracked representations are both used.
Epistemic label FACT means directly observed in source text or deterministic output.
Epistemic label ASSUMPTION means a reasonable inference that requires validation.
Epistemic label PROPOSAL means an agent or tool suggestion requiring human decision.
Epistemic label TBD means an unknown value requiring resolution.
Epistemic labels help separate evidence from inference and prevent plausible invention from becoming project truth.
